title: Branch-gated IaC CI with Conftest evidence and upgrade-safe rollbacks
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Summary:
We need a branch-gated CI pipeline for Terraform modules used in Private (VPC) deployments that enforces linting/formatting, runs deterministic plans, evaluates policy-as-code (Conftest/OPA) against the plan JSON, and produces a verifiable evidence bundle stored with the artifact. The pipeline must also support staged, rollback-safe applies: canary apply, health checks post-apply, and automatic rollback when health metrics degrade beyond thresholds.

Goals:
- Prevent unsafe changes from being merged/applied to Private deployments by failing PRs that violate policy or produce unsafe diffs.
- Provide auditable evidence for compliance teams: plan JSON + Conftest report + signature.
- Ensure upgrades to core Terraform modules can be deployed with a small blast radius and automatic rollback if post-apply health checks fail.

Acceptance criteria (must be met before rolling out to all teams):
1) Every PR modifying terraform/ modules runs: terraform fmt, tflint, terraform init/plan (json output), conftest test against plan JSON.
2) Conftest failures fail the pipeline and post an inline comment on the PR with a summary and link to the full report.
3) The pipeline uploads the plan JSON and conftest report to the artifact store (S3/CI artifacts) with checksum and cosign signature.
4) The apply pipeline supports a canary stage (5% of hosts / 1 VPC) and runs health checks (route checks, service probes, KV cache smoke tests). If health check fails within a 15-minute observation window, automated rollback is triggered.
5) Dashboardable metrics: policy-fail-rate, time-to-merge-after-policy-failure, canary-failure-rate, rollback occurrences.

Design and approach:
1) CI templates: create a reusable pipeline template (GitHub Actions and GitLab CI flavors) placed in infra-ci/. The template has two main flows: PR (plan + policy) and Deploy (canary apply + observe + promote).
2) Plan and policy: run `terraform plan -out=plan.binary && terraform show -json plan.binary > plan.json`. Run `conftest test --policy policies/ --input plan.json --output json` to produce a machine-readable report. Use our Rego policies in policies/vpc/ that encode: disallowed public subnets, open security groups, broad role attachments, change of module major version without approval, and KMS key rotations.
3) Evidence bundle: package `{plan.json, conftest-report.json, pipeline-metadata.json}` and sign with cosign (private key in KMS). Store under s3://redwood-iac-evidence/<repo>/<pr>/<sha>/bundle.tar.gz.sig. Record checksum and signer in CI artifact metadata.
4) Apply safety: Deploy pipeline executes `terraform apply -auto-approve -target=module.<canary_module>` using a canary workspace. After apply, run a health-check playbook (scripts/health_check.sh) that probes endpoints, verifies KV cache warmup, and confirms telemetry forwarding. If checks fail, run `terraform destroy -target=module.<canary_module>` (or run a rollback plan) and send alerts to #infra-alerts with playbook links.
5) Manual approvals: if Plan indicates >X changes to networking topology or >Y IAM changes, require explicit approver group (infra-approvers) before production apply.

Trade-offs and risks:
- Running full plan + conftest in PRs adds CI time (expected +1-3m for init/plan; +0.5-2m for conftest depending on rule complexity). Mitigation: cache plugin downloads, use partial workspaces, and incremental plan heuristics.
- Flaky external provider calls on plan can cause noise. Mitigation: prefer provider mocking for unit tests and run full integration plan in nightly pipelines.
- Evidence signing adds complexity (KMS key rotation), but required for compliance. Start with an opt-in alpha and expand.

Implementation tasks (high level):
- [ ] Create reusable CI templates for PR and Deploy flows (infra-ci/templates/pr.yml, deploy.yml)
- [ ] Author Rego policies for VPC modules (policies/vpc/*) and Conftest wrapper scripts
- [ ] Implement evidence bundling and signing helper (scripts/sign_evidence.sh)
- [ ] Add canary apply stage and health-check playbook (scripts/health_check.sh)
- [ ] Add PR bot integration to post conftest summaries and artifact links
- [ ] Instrument metrics and Grafana dashboard for policy and rollout metrics

Rollout plan:
Alpha: infra team only -- 2 weeks, iterate on false positives and runtime.
Beta: private-deployments teams -- 4 weeks, refine policies and approval thresholds.
GA: org-wide for Private (VPC) modules and infra-owned modules.

Notes on policies: keep Rego rules deterministic and focus on plan JSON structure (change blocks) rather than provider responses. Policies must include a severity field to allow non-blocking warnings vs failures.

Operational runbook (short):
- If a pipeline fails the conftest step, reviewer should triage: is it a valid policy violation or a false positive? Attach PR with `policy:needs-triage` label.
- If canary health-check fails, notifications are sent to #infra-alerts and the pipeline runs rollback; runbooks at internal docs link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/IAC/Canary+Rollback+Runbook
comments: 2025-02-21 | Priya Shah: Initial ticket created after Friday incident where an unapproved module bump caused 3 private VPCs to lose route propagation. Proposed branch-gated approach to prevent recurrence.

2025-02-23 | Diego Martinez: Spike completed for Conftest against plan.json. Prototype rules located at repo: github.com/redwood-inference/infra-policies PR #412 (https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-policies/pull/412). Observations: plan.json has provider-specific noise; will normalize using helper to strip timestamps and provider meta.

2025-02-25 | Aisha Patel (Security review): Reviewed initial Rego set. Requested that any change touching KMS keys or role policies be auto-marked 'high-impact' and require two approvers. Also requested audit evidence be pushed to the WORM bucket for 90 days retention.

2025-02-27 | Diego Martinez: Implemented evidence signer `scripts/sign_evidence.sh` using KMS-wrapped cosign key. Hooked into GitHub Actions artifact upload. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-ci/pull/58. Pipeline time for PR flows increased from 90s to ~210s on first run; subsequent runs 120s with caching.

2025-03-01 | Priya Shah: Decided to gate high-impact changes (networking/IAM/KMS) behind manual approvers. For medium-impact changes, we'll auto-fail the PR but allow admins to override via explicit label `infra:force-apply` with audit log. Added to acceptance criteria.
2025-03-01 | Diego Martinez: Next steps: add canary apply helper and health-check scripts, instrument metrics for policy failure rates, and schedule alpha rollout with infra team on 2025-03-10.

2025-03-01 | QA note (Liam O'Connor): Will prepare two test repos: one with deliberate policy violations (open sg) and one simulating safe module bump. Will validate automatic evidence upload and signature verification.
2025-03-01 | PR checklist: requires at least one infra approver, 1 security reviewer for policies, e2e pipeline run in staging that signs evidence and performs a dry-run canary apply.
